issues.legal_issue: A purchaser is not in default for failing to complete a sale while the vendor’s title remains incomplete or required transfer approval has not been obtained and communicated as agreed.
material_facts: The vendors’ lease deed had not been executed when the sale agreement was made, and transfer of the plot required government approval.
The parties agreed that the sale deed would be executed after the approval was obtained and that the vendors would inform the purchasers when it was received.
The vendors obtained approval but did not inform the purchasers, who had sought the approval and remained ready to pay the balance when the agreed conditions were met.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers had not failed to perform within a reasonable time, and the vendors’ letters did not make time the essence of the contract.
issues.legal_principle: A purchaser cannot be required to complete a sale while the vendor’s title is incomplete or an agreed prerequisite to completion remains unmet. Where the vendor has undertaken to notify the purchaser after obtaining the required approval, the vendor cannot treat the purchaser as in default without giving that notice. The court rejected the application of the time-essential reasoning under the Specific Relief Act raised in the proceedings.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and vendor_title_incomplete and transfer_approval_required and agreement_defers_completion_until_approval and vendor_did_not_notify_approval

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.vendor_title_incomplete: The vendor had not yet obtained complete title to the property.
predicates.transfer_approval_required: A third party’s approval was required before the property could be transferred.
predicates.agreement_defers_completion_until_approv: The parties agreed that completion would occur only after the required approval was obtained.
predicates.vendor_did_not_notify_approval: The vendor obtained the approval but did not notify the purchaser as agreed.

issues.definition: If a purchaser seeks specific performance and the vendor’s title or required approval remains incomplete, with completion deferred until approval and no notice given after it is obtained, the purchaser is not in default.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser’s readiness and willingness to perform must be assessed from the entirety of the relevant facts and conduct, rather than by a fixed formula.
material_facts: The purchasers informed prospective buyers that the plot was subject to their agreement and made inquiries about the required approval.

They wrote that they would pay the balance once the vendors obtained the approval, and they promptly sued for specific performance after learning that approval had been granted without notice to them.
The purchasers had paid the earnest money, had funds available, and were carrying on a business from which they could arrange any remaining balance.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were ready and willing to perform their part of the contract.
issues.legal_principle: Readiness and willingness are not determined by a straight-jacket formula; they must be assessed from the entirety of the facts and circumstances relevant to the party’s intention and conduct. The court treated specific performance as discretionary relief, but discretion must be exercised according to sound and reasonable judicial principles rather than arbitrarily. The Specific Relief Act provisions raised at trial were sections 21 and 22; no earlier case was relied on for this readiness-and-willingness principle.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_affirmed_willingness_to_pay and purchaser_protected_contract_interest and purchaser_promptly_sought_enforcement and purchaser_could_arrange_balance

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.purchaser_affirmed_willingness_to_pay: The purchaser communicated willingness to pay the balance when the agreed conditions for completion were met.
predicates.purchaser_protected_contract_interest: The purchaser took steps such as informing prospective buyers of the agreement or inquiring about a required approval.
predicates.purchaser_promptly_sought_enforcement: The purchaser promptly brought proceedings to enforce the agreement after learning that completion could proceed.
predicates.purchaser_could_arrange_balance: The purchaser had funds or a demonstrated ability to arrange the balance of the purchase price.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance has affirmed willingness to pay, protected the contract interest, promptly sought enforcement, and could arrange the balance, the purchaser is ready and willing.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser’s challenge to the refusal of specific performance is not barred by a monetary decree’s satisfaction when the purchaser’s consistent conduct shows that the decree was not accepted as correct.
material_facts: The trial court refused specific performance but ordered the earnest money returned.
The vendors deposited the amount in satisfaction of that decree during the appeal, and the purchasers did not withdraw it.
The purchasers had sought an injunction against disposal of the property and prosecuted an appeal seeking specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were not precluded from obtaining specific performance by the deposit or purported satisfaction of the monetary decree.
issues.legal_principle: A party ordinarily cannot approbate and reprobate by accepting a judgment’s benefit while appealing on the basis that the judgment is wrong. But that principle did not bar relief where the party’s consistent and unequivocal conduct showed that it did not accept the judgment as correct. The court referred to Dexters, Limited v. Hill Crest Oil Company Bradford Ltd. [1926] 1 K.B. 348, 358, for the general rule against accepting a judgment’s benefit while appealing against it.

predicates.appeal_against_refusal_of_specific_perfo: A purchaser appealed from a decree refusing specific performance.
predicates.monetary_decree_satisfied_or_amount_depo: The amount ordered to be returned by the trial court was paid or deposited in satisfaction of that decree.
predicates.purchaser_did_not_withdraw_amount: The purchaser did not withdraw the returned amount while the appeal was pending.
predicates.purchaser_consistently_challenged_refusa: The purchaser took steps to prevent disposal of the property and pursued an appeal seeking specific performance.

issues.definition: When a purchaser appeals the refusal of specific performance, does not withdraw the amount paid or deposited under the monetary decree, and consistently challenges the refusal, satisfaction of that decree does not bar specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: When property subject to an agreement of sale has been transferred to a subsequent transferee, the decree for specific performance may direct that transferee to join in the conveyance to pass title to the purchaser.
material_facts: The vendors had transferred the property to a subsequent transferee before the decree for specific performance was made.
issues.conclusion: The decree should direct specific performance between the vendors and the purchasers and require the subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance to pass on the title held by that transferee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Lal Durga Prasad v. Lala Deep Chand, [1954] S.C.R. 360, the decree may direct the subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance so as to pass the title residing in that transferee to the purchaser. The transferee does not join in any special covenants between the purchaser and the vendor; the transferee’s role is to pass on the title.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.property_transferred_to_subsequent_trans: The vendor transferred the property to another person after entering the agreement with the purchaser.

issues.definition: When specific performance is sought and the property has been transferred to another person, the subsequent transferee must join in the conveyance to pass the title held by that transferee.
